hero.title: Did that bus run on schedule?
hero.lead: We collect every public GTFS-RT (real-time operations) feed in Japan every minute and match it trip by trip against the published timetable — a third-party record that doesn't depend on any contract with the operator.

councils.title: Audit report
councils.body: Were subsidized and contracted routes operated as planned? We put each route's confirmation rate and on-time rate into the shape of a quarterly council packet.

operators.title: Data quality
operators.body: Every GTFS-RT feed graded A through F each month on freshness and coverage, so you can see which routes and hours are going missing.

observatory.heading: Grading Japan's real-time bus feeds, every month.
observatory.lead: We watch every public real-time bus feed we can find. No contract with the operator required. Each month we grade every one, A through F, on freshness and coverage.
observatory.footnote: On-time rate is the share of trips that departed less than {{seconds}} seconds behind schedule. The monthly grade scores the feed itself — a separate measure from how well the buses actually ran.

councils.heading: A report your council packet can use as-is.
councils.lead: We sum up whether subsidized and contracted routes ran as planned, in a third party's own numbers. The source, the definitions and the timetable version are footnoted automatically.

report.title: Operating performance of subsidized routes
report.footnote: Source: GTFS-RT published by each operator (collected every minute), matched against the GTFS timetable (the {{timetableDate}} edition), compiled independently by this service. On-time means under {{seconds}}s behind schedule (definition v{{version}}). The {{unobserved}} unobserved trips are excluded from the denominator and listed in Table A.

method.heading: Every number's origin, shown in full.
method.lead: Collect, compare, publish — the same three steps, and the same definitions, everywhere in Japan.
method.step1_body: We fetch public GTFS-RT every minute and keep whatever arrives as-is. A minute we couldn't fetch is recorded too, not skipped over.
method.step2_body: We compare the time each trip actually passed a stop against the GTFS timetable's scheduled time, stop by stop.
method.step3_body: We publish the definitions, the formulas and the timetable version. Anyone who recalculates gets the same number.
method.honesty_gaps: Gaps in collection, shown in gray

bustown.heading: Watch a city's whole day, bus by moving bus.
bustown.body: The record of buses that actually ran, played back on the route map. Green is on time; yellow to orange is late. Watch the colors shift through rush hour.

footer.disclaimer: This service independently aggregates data each operator publishes; it is not an operator's official information. Every figure on this page is a sample.

delay.title: What a delay is here
delay.body: A delay is how many minutes after its timetable a bus left a stop, as the operator's own real-time feed reports it. Each departure from a stop counts once, and an early departure counts as a negative delay. The large figure is the average of those departures over the period.

on_time.title: What on time means
on_time.body: A departure is on time when it leaves between {{early}} early and {{late}} late. Leaving earlier than that is not on time. This screen shows average delay; the on-time rate is on Routes and on each route's page.
on_time.body_any_early: A departure is on time when it leaves no more than {{late}} late, and every early departure counts as on time too. This screen shows average delay; the on-time rate is on Routes and on each route's page.

scope.title: What this screen covers
scope.body: This sentence says which routes, days and hours are counted, and over which period. Pulse compares that period with the same number of days just before it. Click any part marked ▼ to change it.

network.title: Compare agencies
network.help_avg_delay: Typical lateness in minutes over the window; the dot shows severity.
network.help_on_time: Share of observations within the on-time threshold. The range shown with it is its 95% interval, counted over trips rather than observations, since the stops of one trip run late together.
network.help_delivered: Share of planned trips that ran without being reported cancelled. Shown only for agencies whose feed a check has confirmed can carry cancellations and that reported at least one in the period or the 90 days up to its end; otherwise "—" with the reason.
network.help_samples: Number of delay observations behind the figures.
network.help_feed: Percent of readings dropped as implausible — high means a stuck or frozen feed.
network.help_freshness: Whether the figures include the latest ingested data. "Behind" means the precomputed totals haven't caught up yet, so the most recent days may be missing.
network.help_coverage: The date span this agency actually has data for within the window.
network.help_ridership_weighted: When a manually-configured ridership weight exists for this agency, pools each route's on-time contribution by that weight instead of counting every route equally.
network.help_vehicle_km_delivered: Service delivered % applied to the current timetable's planned vehicle-kilometres. Shown only where Service delivered % is; "—" when no route shapes (shapes.txt) are loaded.
network.plan_coverage_footnote: * Where Planned trips reads “N/M days a timetable plans”, that agency's Planned trips, Service delivered % and Vehicle-km delivered % count only the days a timetable plans. Only part of the period has a plan, so those figures cover fewer days than other agencies'.
network.help_planned_trips: The trips the timetable planned to run over the period, from each day's saved count or the loaded timetable.

network.help_observed_coverage: Trips the feed reported as a share of the trips the timetable planned, on the days it plans up to the newest day any agency has observations for. Over 100% means the feed reported trips the timetable doesn't name.
network.help_ranking: Only the agencies whose data supports a comparison are ranked: observation coverage of at least {{coverage}}%, an on-time % interval within ±{{ci}} points, and implausible readings of at most {{clamp}}%. The rest follow by name, each with the first check it fails. Every agency's on-time % uses the industry standard (no more than 1 min early or 5 min late). Neither how densely a feed reports nor where a timetable puts its slack is corrected for.

network.unranked_criteria: Ranked only where observation coverage is at least {{coverage}}%, the on-time % interval is within ±{{ci}} points and implausible readings are at most {{clamp}}%. These are listed by name.

dedupRule.latest_observation_per_stop_event: When a departure is reported more than once, the latest report counts, unless it arrives more than 130 minutes after the scheduled departure; then the last report before that counts.

overview.concentration_explainer: Each route's share of the delay summed over the routes counted in the selected range. Route codes the current timetable no longer runs, and routes whose feed always reports zero delay, are not counted. The Lorenz curve below shows the skew: the dotted diagonal would be a perfectly even spread, and the further the curve bows away from it, the more the delay sits with a few routes.

avg_delay.title: Average delay
avg_delay.body: The mean of every departure delay in the period, in minutes: how late each bus left each stop against its timetable. Early departures stay in the mean as negative delays.

peak_hour.title: Heaviest hour
peak_hour.body: The hour of the day whose departures had the highest average delay over the period, under the conditions above. The row opens Time, which shows every hour by day.

concentration.title: Share of delay
concentration.body: Of all the minutes departures left late in the period, the share these routes account for. Early departures count as zero. The higher the share, the more the delay sits with a few routes.

late_routes.title: Routes averaging late
late_routes.body: How many routes averaged at least {{min}} min late over the period, out of the routes observed {{floor}} or more times. A route observed fewer times is left out, since a handful of trips can swing its average, as are the routes Routes leaves out by default: retired route codes and feeds that always report zero delay.

routes_to_check.title: Routes to check
routes_to_check.body: The first rows of the Routes table for these days: the routes with the highest average delay, among the routes observed {{floor}} or more times, leaving out the routes Routes leaves out by default (retired route codes and feeds that always report zero delay). Click a route to open its page, or the link below for every route.

routeReference.legend: “Better”, “About the same” and “Worse” beside an on-time rate compare it with the route’s own past {{days}} days ({{range}}). Point at one for the past {{days}} days’ rate. Routes observed fewer than {{min}} times in those days have none.
routeReference.not_aggregated_band: With a time of day chosen, routes are not compared with their past {{days}} days.
routeReference.not_aggregated_window: The chosen on-time window is not aggregated, so routes are not compared with their past {{days}} days.
routeReference.hint_body: Each route’s on-time rate and average delay over the {{days}} days before the period ({{range}}), under the same conditions as the figures (days of the week, timetable and routes) and the same on-time definition. {{coverage}}A difference under {{flat_pp}} point in the on-time rate reads “about the same”, and a higher rate is better. An average delay is judged by the same rule as Pulse’s comparison with the past {{days}} days: a difference under {{flat_min}} min, or under {{flat_pct}}% of the past {{days}} days’ average, reads “about the same”, and a shorter delay is better; when either average is below 0 min (departures running early), it is not judged better or worse. With a time of day chosen, or an on-time window that is not aggregated, nothing is compared.
routeReference.hint_coverage: They are shown when the feed has data on at least {{min_days}} of the {{selected}} days those conditions select and the route has at least {{min_samples}} observations.
